newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel took a tough line on Wednesday against Western Cape government pleas for an increase in its budget allocation, despite warnings that the 780 million rand cut would mean a drastic pruning of social services and the loss of thousands of public servants' jobs.

- South African gold sales were under-reported by a quarter last year after the Central Statistical Service (CSS) was fed incorrect information by the Minerals Bureau, which omitted key Rand Refinery toll refining figures.

- Government joined parliamentarians on Wednesday in expressing concern about its 134.8 billion rand contingent liabilities, which include the underfunding of the Multilateral Motor Vehicle Accident Fund.

- International mediation of constitutional differences was no longer politically practical and the Inkatha Freedom Party's demand for it had been abandoned, the party conceded on Wednesday while insisting it would still be raised as a point of honour.

- Financial services group Norwich Holdings SA Ltd lifted attributable earnings 35 percent to 84 million rand in the year to December, its maiden year as a listed group, following strong performances from its life and asset management and unit trust companies.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Sasol Ltd, the South African synthetic fuel from coal producer, plans to build a multi-billion rand plant in the Gulf state of Qatar to convert natural gas to liquid fuels, it said on Wednesday.

- A boardroom drama, tainted with speculation of sackings, resignations and stony silences, faces Sentrachem Ltd management barely two weeks after the 4,9 billion rand company announced it would post first-half losses.

- Project Buxie, an undercover initiative between the private sector and the South African Police Services (SAPS), could provide the only hope of combating growing container theft in Durban, Yvonne Lowe, the chief executive of Roadwing, a Johannesburg-based freight company, said on Wednesday.
- British Airways BAB.L Comair is withdrawing from the cape Town to Windhoek routes from April 14 and is moving passengers who have already booked to other carriers, the airline said on Wednesday.

- The National Empowerment Trust (NET), a new black empowerment organisation led by entrepreneur Don Mkhwanazi, was officially launched on Wednesday, following the recent announcement of two projects already concluded with Malaysian partners.
THE STAR

- Well-organised, heavily armed gangs, striking with military precision in Johannesburg's affluent northern suburbs, are using increasingly violent tactics to subdue their victims, and police fear that attacks are on the increase.
- The Gauteng government has announced plans to speed up the placement of abandoned babies in hospitals.

- Truth and Reconciliation Commission chairman Archbishop Desmond Tutu announced on Wednesday that his prostate cancer appeared to have spread and that he would undergo radiotherapy in the United States.

- A 21-year-old man convicted of murdering his family's domestic worker has appealed against a sentence of three years' correctional supervision which was handed down in the Johannesburg Regional Court on Wednesday.
- A revised contract between Mpumalanga's Park Board and the controversial Dubai-based Dolphin Group was unanimously ratified by the board's directors on Wednesday night in Nelspruit.
